---
title: "Design Lab: A News Feed with Fan-Out and Cursors"
---

# Design Lab: A News Feed with Fan-Out and Cursors

Build a chronological Go feed before adding ranking. The difficult part is maintaining a useful materialized view while follows, deletes, and privacy rules change. A cached feed entry never grants permission to read the underlying post.

## API and durable model

Implement `POST /posts`, idempotent `PUT /follows/{author}`, and `GET /feed?cursor=...&limit=...`. Store posts, follow edges, and an outbox event in PostgreSQL. Start with fan-out on read: query followed authors and order by `(created_at DESC, id DESC)`.

Use a cursor containing both ordering fields and the account it belongs to. An illustrative query fragment is:

```sql
SELECT p.id, p.author_id, p.created_at, p.body
FROM posts p
JOIN follows f ON f.author_id = p.author_id
WHERE f.reader_id = $1
  AND (p.created_at, p.id) < ($2, $3)
ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC
LIMIT $4;
```

This assumes follow uniqueness and a non-null total-order tuple. Apply visibility rules as part of authorized retrieval; a production schema needs those predicates too. Bound the page size in Go. Treat timestamps as ordering fields, not proof of causal order across machines.

## Grow to fan-out on write

Build a worker that reads the post outbox and inserts `(reader_id, post_id)` into feed entries under a uniqueness constraint. This shifts work to publishing and makes reads cheap. Record the high-water mark and delivery lag; a successful publish can precede feed visibility.

For an author with a million followers, one post creates a million writes. Use bounded batches and resumable checkpoints. A hybrid design precomputes normal authors and merges high-fan-out authors at read time. The author threshold is a measured operational choice.

In Go, load candidate IDs in bounded pages, batch-fetch posts, and recheck current authorization before rendering. Avoid one goroutine and query per feed entry. An unfollow, private-account change, or deletion must take effect even if background cleanup has not removed every cached candidate.

## Failure and pagination evidence

Publish once, replay the outbox twice, and assert one feed entry per reader. Pause the worker, keep publishing, and demonstrate eventual catch-up without unbounded heap growth. Delete or privatize a post while it remains cached and assert it cannot be returned.

Insert posts between page requests and verify stable keyset pagination without repeated items in the unchanged dataset. Document that a live feed is not a frozen snapshot unless you add a snapshot boundary. Measure publish latency, fan-out backlog age, database rows read per page, and p99 feed latency under one celebrity author. Explain when the hybrid design improves those measurements and what consistency it sacrifices.
